text:
sanjeev: :rotating_light: seeing a large uptick in 401s from hosted API around 11:02 UTC. Lots of customers reporting auth failures right after the automated key rotation job ran. Not seeing obvious errors downstream yet.

ops-bot: Alert: auth-service: 5xxs and 401 spike detected between 11:01-11:05 UTC. Rolling 1m averages crossed threshold.

maya: confirmed, dashboards show JWKS fetch latency spiking then 500s from jwks.redwood.internal during the rotation window. Can anyone confirm if the rotation job changed the jwks endpoint behavior?

ian (support): multiple support tickets — customers seeing `401 invalid_token` for both API key and OAuth flows. Some SSO logins failing with `token introspection error`. Escalating to ops.

anna (sre): digging into rotation job logs. The key-flip job completed but the auth-proxy cache TTL was not invalidated. We served a mix of old and new keys for a short window; however jwks endpoint started returning 500 after backend B went unhealthy. Suspect a timing issue where backend B was removed while rotation created a new key set that depended on it.

maya: snapshot of jwks endpoint at 11:03: 
```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"failed to load keyset","details":"KMS call timed out"}
```

sanjeev: can we force the auth-proxy to fall back to cached certs and stop returning 500s? What is the safe rollback path for the key flip?

anna (sre): two immediate mitigations: 1) bounce the auth-proxy instance that lost KMS access to trigger it to re-fetch with fallback to previous in-memory keys, 2) temporarily disable the new key in the routing layer so only old key is used. Doing (2) now via route config.

infra-bot: Executed: `PATCH /config/auth/routing` set `active_key: previous` by anna (sre).

maya: after routing rollback, jwks endpoint returned 200 but we still see sporadic 401s — looks like CDN edge caches holding the bad jwks for a short TTL. Clearing edge caches for /.well-known/jwks.json across regions.

ian (support): Messaging to affected customers: "We're investigating an authentication disruption affecting certain API keys and OAuth tokens. Working on mitigation now and will follow up with timeline and remediation steps."

sanjeev: reproduction steps for engineers trying to validate fix: 
1) curl the jwks endpoint: `curl -sv https://jwks-internal.redwood/v1/jwks` 
2) generate a token signed with the new key material (if you have access) and attempt an authenticated request. 
3) look for `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error=\"invalid_token\"` in responses.

anna (sre): logs from auth-proxy around 11:02 show KMS timeouts and then a panic in key loader that is caught but returns 500 upstream: 
```
[11:02:13] ERROR keyloader.go:128 failed to fetch keyset: context deadline exceeded (KMS call)
[11:02:13] WARN http: returning 500 to /v1/jwks
```

maya: root cause hypothesis: the key rotation job increased KMS request concurrency; one backend lost network path to KMS (transient routing flapping), key loader didn't have a robust fallback ordering and returned errors instead of serving prior keyset from disk. Also CDN caching prolonged customer impact.

sanjeev: next steps we agreed on: 
- anna to harden keyloader fallback order + add local disk fallback (PR in flight).
- infra to add a short canary window and health check gate for jwks after rotation (so rotation waits for jwks 200 across backends).
- maya to scope CDN TTL change for jwks to 10s and purge on rotation.
- support (ian) to send post-mortem update to impacted customers with timeline and credits.

anna (sre): PR opened: `fix/keyloader-fallback` — adds disk fallback + retries + better metrics. Will also add a KMS concurrency limiter.

infra-bot: Created incident postmortem draft at /incidents/1769456789/jwks-rotation-regression (private).

ian (support): noted. Drafting customer comms now. Will include exact start/stop times and recommended steps for customers who tried to rotate their own keys.

maya: followup check — verify all affected tenants have had tokens revalidated. I ran a smoke test against 5 high-traffic tenants and tokens accepted now. Please watch latency/401 dashboards for next 2h.

sanjeev: thanks everyone. After-token fix, monitor and close when stable. Add retro items to platform backlog for canary gating and CDN purge automation. :thumbsup:
